ig_caption:
Stuck below 1000? Look out for hope chess.

A hope move is one that only works if your opponent misses something: a threat that is easy to stop, or a piece left loose. It wins some games against new players, and loses more and more as your opponents get better.

The fix is one question before every move: what is their best reply? Not their likely reply, their best one. Early queen raids at f7 are the classic example. When you can't find a real attack, make a quiet, useful move instead: castle, improve a piece, take an open file.

slides.title: Stuck below 1000?
slides.sub: MOVES THAT ONLY WORK IF THEY MISS IT

slides.title: What is hope chess?
slides.body: You make a move and hope your opponent won't see the problem: a threat that is easy to stop, or a piece left loose. Sometimes it works.
slides.note: As your opponents get better, it works less and less.

slides.title: Ask: what is their best reply?
slides.body: Not their likely reply. Their best one. If your move only works when they make a mistake, it is a hope move.
slides.note: Picture the reply that hurts you most. Then decide.

slides.title: The early queen raid
slides.body: Bringing the queen out early to aim at f7 wins quick games against new players. A calm defender blocks it, then chases your queen while bringing out pieces.
slides.note: If they defend well and you end up worse, it was hope.

slides.title: No attack? Play a useful move
slides.body: When you can't find a real threat, make your position better instead: castle, move a knight to a stronger square, put a rook on an open file.
slides.note: Quiet, solid moves win more games than cheap tricks.

slides.title: Every lucky win is on the poster.
slides.sub: Your whole rating history, on one print.
